description: What each rules domain fixes: the commitment TTL an issuer must use, and the settlement profile the domain settles under. Both are decisions on the hot path — the TTL gates acceptance at submit, the profile selects how a settlement is read back — so two implementations that disagree on either reject each other's perfectly valid material. This vector pins both.

rules.commitment_ttl_seconds: expires_at MUST equal issued_at + this, exactly. It is not an upper bound: an issuer cannot shorten its own window either, or the TTL would say nothing about how long evidence stays valid.
rules.unknown_rules_version: null on BOTH columns, and null means REFUSE. An unrecognized domain is not a domain with defaults: accepting it under some fallback would admit material nobody can settle.
rules.note_on_profile: Every domain in this table settles under the same profile. That is not an invariant: the column exists because a domain may settle under another profile, and an implementation must read it rather than assume.

scope_note: This table lists the rules domains a third party can encounter. A deployment may run domains of its own that are not here; a verifier resolves those from the configuration it is given, never from this table. An unknown domain answers null on both columns, and that is a refusal — not an invitation to guess a default.
